title: Arizona LLC for Non-Residents: Cost and Steps (2026)
h1: How to Form an Arizona LLC as a Non-Resident (2026 Cost and Steps)
description: How non-US founders form an Arizona LLC in 2026: $50 articles, no annual report, the publication rule, an Arizona statutory agent, EIN and Form 5472.
llms_summary: A non-resident can form an Arizona LLC for a $50 Arizona Corporation Commission fee, must keep an Arizona statutory agent who accepts in writing, may need to publish a notice of formation, and files no LLC annual report.
body_html:
Short answer: Anyone can form an Arizona LLC from abroad, with no US citizenship, residency or visa. You file articles of organization with the Arizona Corporation Commission for $50, along with a signed acceptance from an Arizona statutory agent, then get an EIN from the IRS. Arizona's LLC fee schedule has no annual report, so there is no yearly state report fee. The two Arizona rules to plan for are the statutory agent acceptance and the requirement to publish a notice of formation.

What Arizona charges

The Arizona Corporation Commission's LLC fee schedule (revised March 2026) and Arizona Revised Statutes section 29-3213 set these fees. All fees are nonrefundable.

  • Articles of organization: $50, or $85 with expedited handling.
  • Annual report: none. The LLC fee schedule and the fee statute list no LLC annual report.
  • Statement of change of principal address or statutory agent: $5.
  • Articles of amendment: $25.
  • Articles of termination: $35.
  • Application for reinstatement: $100, plus other fees and penalties due.
  • Registering an LLC formed in another state: $150.
  • Certificate of good standing: $10.
  • EIN: free from the IRS.

The Commission also lists faster paid services: next day for $100, same day for $200 and two-hour service for $400. Commercial statutory agent fees are extra and set by each provider.

Step by step

  1. Check the name in the Commission's eCorp business search.
  2. Choose a statutory agent. An individual agent must be a permanent, full-time Arizona resident with a physical street address in Arizona. A company agent must be authorized to do business in Arizona. The LLC cannot be its own agent.
  3. Get the agent's written acceptance on the Commission's Statutory Agent Acceptance form. The Commission's instructions say articles are rejected if no acceptance is on file when they are examined, so send it with the articles.
  4. File the articles of organization with a cover sheet and the member or manager structure attachment.
  5. Publish the notice of formation if required (see below), but only after the Commission approves the articles.
  6. Sign an operating agreement. It is kept by the company, not filed, and banks often ask for it.
  7. Get an EIN with Form SS-4, then open a bank account.

The publication rule

Arizona requires a notice of the filing of the articles to be published under section 29-3201. The Commission's instructions say that if the statutory agent's street address is in Maricopa or Pima county, the Commission publishes the notice on its own website automatically. If the agent is in any other county, you must publish the notice in a newspaper yourself. Many founders abroad pick an agent in Phoenix (Maricopa) or Tucson (Pima) for this reason. Check the Commission's current instructions for the deadline before you file.

Privacy: what is public

Arizona is less private than some states. The articles must list the LLC's structure: a member-managed LLC lists at least one member, and a manager-managed LLC lists at least one manager plus any member who owns 20% or more. Those names go on the public record. If owner privacy matters to you, compare Wyoming or New Mexico.

Keep your agent current

The Commission's instructions say an LLC that does not keep a valid statutory agent address can be administratively dissolved. With no annual report to remind you, this is the main way an Arizona LLC is lost from abroad. Keep the agent paid and file a $5 statement of change whenever the agent or address changes.

Paying from abroad

The Commission's instructions say it does not accept checks drawn on non-US banks, and they describe card payments as Visa or Mastercard only. Check the payment options on eCorp before you file, or use a formation service that pays the state fee for you.

Federal steps for non-resident owners

  • EIN: if you have no SSN or ITIN, you enter "foreign" on line 7b of Form SS-4 and apply by fax, mail or the IRS international phone line. See how to get an EIN without an SSN.
  • Form 5472: a single-member LLC owned by a non-US person files Form 5472 with a pro forma Form 1120 each year, even with no income. See Form 5472 for foreign-owned LLCs.
  • BOI: LLCs formed in the US, including Arizona LLCs, are exempt from FinCEN beneficial ownership reporting. See BOI reporting in 2026.

Arizona state taxes depend on what you sell and where. Check the Arizona Department of Revenue's guidance if you have customers, stock or staff in the state.

Statutory agent address vs business address

The statutory agent address is where legal notices go. It is not automatically your business or mailing address. Banks and payment providers usually ask for a business address and for each owner's real personal residential address, which for most non-residents is their home abroad. Many banks decline CMRA or virtual mailbox addresses as a business address, so check the bank's eligibility page first. See what a CMRA address is.

Arizona vs Wyoming or Delaware

Arizona has one of the lowest formation fees and no annual report, so the long-run state cost is low. The trade-offs are the publication rule and owner names on the articles. It fits best if you have customers, staff or a warehouse in Arizona. For a remote online business, also compare Wyoming vs Delaware.

The Residential Address forms Arizona LLCs for non-US founders, including the EIN application. See LLC formation.

faqs: Can a non-US citizen form an Arizona LLC?

Yes. Arizona has no citizenship or residency requirement for LLC owners. You need a statutory agent who is an Arizona resident with an Arizona street address, or a company authorized to do business in Arizona.
How much does an Arizona LLC cost to form?
The articles of organization cost $50, or $85 with expedited handling, under the Arizona Corporation Commission fee schedule. Statutory agent fees are extra.
Does an Arizona LLC file an annual report?
No. The Commission's LLC fee schedule and the fee statute list no LLC annual report. You must keep a valid statutory agent at all times.
Do I have to publish a notice for an Arizona LLC?

A notice of formation is required. If your statutory agent's street address is in Maricopa or Pima county, the Commission publishes it on its website automatically. Otherwise you publish it in a newspaper after the articles are approved.
Are owner names public for an Arizona LLC?
Often yes. The articles list at least one member or manager, and a manager-managed LLC must also list any member who owns 20% or more.
